key_messages: Unsettled weather pattern continues for today with showers likely, before drier weather returns for Wednesday.
The probability (55%-80%) of a widespread precipitation event has increased Thursday into Friday with some wet snow accumulation possible for the higher terrain, exact impacts still to be determined.
Seasonably cool and trending drier through the weekend into early next week.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
147 AM EST Tue Nov 10 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 142 AM EST Tuesday...

No significant changes made.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 142 AM EST Tuesday...

1. Unsettled weather pattern continues for today with showers 
likely, before drier weather returns for Wednesday.  

2. The probability (55%-80%) of a widespread precipitation 
event has increased Thursday into Friday with some wet snow 
accumulation possible for the higher terrain, exact impacts still to 
be determined. 
  
3. Seasonably cool and trending drier through the weekend into 
early next week. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 142 AM EST Tuesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: GOES-19 water vapor imagery is indicating compact s/w 
energy over the northern Great Lakes this morning, which wl dive 
southeast toward our cwa today. This mid lvl forcing, combined with 
a pocket of enhanced 850 to 500mb moisture and developing 925mb to 
850mb northwest upslope flow wl help produce areas of showers, 
especially this aftn. Greatest probabilities (80-95%) wl be over the 
favorable upslope areas of the northern dacks and central/northern 
Greens btwn 18z and 00z today. Progged rh fields show deepest 
moisture/lift near the International Border and mtns today, with 
much less favorable dynamics and moisture over southern VT. Did note 
a weak pocket of instability over the SLV with MUCAPE of 150-300 
J/kg, which per the progged HRRR composite reflectivity could 
produce a few embedded heavier convective element with maybe some 
graupel. Snow level wl be near summit level, given 850mb temps near 
0C with minimal impacts anticipated. Highs generally range from the 
mid 30s summits to lower 50s warmer valleys under mostly cloudy 
skies. No impactful wx is anticipated tonight into Weds with temps 
hovering near normal.

KEY MESSAGE 2: A strong synoptic scale system is expected to produce a 
widespread precip event acrs our cwa Thursday into Friday with some 
wet snow possible over the higher terrain, but potential 
hazards/impacts still to be determined. 00z guidance, including
the GFS ensemble and associated AI-GFS prog a deepening and 
closing off full latitude trof over the Mid Atlantic/NE CONUS 
late Thurs into Friday. Meanwhile initial sfc low tracks from 
the Ohio Valley on Thurs morning and redevelops over the Mid 
Atlantic/SNE coast by Thurs aftn. The primary issue for snow 
lovers like myself is the lack of cold air initially, especially
with no arctic or modified arctic high pres located to our 
north/northeast. So we are going to need very high precip rates 
to help bring slightly cooler air toward the sfc and elevation 
to see accumulating snowfall, especially with bl temps btwn 2-3C
per latest GFS sounding data at BTV. Sounding data indicates 
very marginal thermal profiles, especially on Thursday with 
progged 850mb temps hovering near 0C and 925mb 0 to 1C, which 
supports snow levels above 3000 feet and minimal impacts. 
However, as system pulls away, winds shift to the northwest and 
llvl caa develops on backside, allowing thermal profiles to cool
and support some accumulating snowfall. The challenge is how 
quickly does the cooler air advect on backside and does moisture
linger around to support accumulation snowfall. At this time, 
the highest probability (60-80%) of several inches of 
accumulating snowfall would be acrs the Dacks and Green mtns of 
VT, Thurs night thru Friday. GFS is very slow with lifting 
mid/upper lvl circulation eastward with sfc weakness/invert trof
lingering into Saturday. This idea would support additional 
snowfall possible, especially trrn. For now have high 
probability of precip (55-80%) for most of our cwa Thurs into 
Friday with some (1-3") wet snow accumulation acrs the High 
Peaks and Spine of the Green Mountains. Temps wl be trending at 
or slightly below normal by Friday with highs upper 20s summits 
to lower 40s valleys and lows mid 20s to mid 30s.

KEY MESSAGE 3: Upper level troughing will prevail for much of the 
weekend, leading to a mostly cloudy and cool stretch. Upslope 
showers are likely Saturday, potentially lingering part of the way 
into Sunday. However, any organized synoptic precipitation will be 
done. Snow levels currently look to be somewhere around 1,000 ft, 
but they could make it all the way down into the Champlain Valley 
during heavier showers or at night when it is cooler. Several 
inches will be possible in the mountains, but anything in the 
valleys would likely be lighter and have a hard time accumulating. 
NBM probabilities of 3+ inches are in the 20-40 percent range in the 
mountains, but these are likely underdone as its long range 
components are too coarse to fully depict terrain effects and 
relevant static stability. Heading into next week, a large surface 
high pressure looks to build into the region, bringing increasing 
sunshine and slightly moderating temperatures.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Through 06Z Wednesday...A mix of MVFR and VFR conditions currently
exist due to low ceilings and they should trend relatively steady
for the rest of the night, though there will be some minor bouncing
up and down. SLK is an outlier and will likely drop into the IFR
range at times with ceilings forming in the 600-900 FT range. A few
showers and areas of drizzle will be around but they are not
expected to significantly lower visibility, except at SLK where some
light snow could mix in and reduce the visibility into the MVFR
range. During the day today, ceilings will trend up a bit, and most
terminals should reach VFR. Scattered slightly heavier showers will
move through during the afternoon and evening, and a brief drop to
MVFR visibility will be possible at any terminal. Heading into the
evening, ceilings will drop slightly, but still range in the MVFR to
VFR range. Winds will be northwesterly to westerly for the rest of
the night, becoming westerly to southwesterly for the day today.
Gusts in the 10-20 KT range are expected today, with gusts up to 25
KT possible.

Outlook...

Veterans Day: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Slight chance
SHRA.
Wednesday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Slight
chance SHRA, Slight chance SHSN.
Thursday: Mainly IFR, with areas MVFR possible. Slight chance
SHRA.
Thursday Night: Mainly IFR, with local MVFR possible. Chance RA,
Chance SN.
Friday: Mainly IFR, with areas MVFR possible. Chance RA, Chance
SN.
Friday Night: MVFR. Chance SN, Chance RA.
Saturday: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Chance SHRA,
Chance SHSN.
